newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FALDO AND CLARKE MISS OUT ON BIRDIE BINGE AT WINGED FOOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO AND CLARKE MISS OUT ON BIRDIE BINGE AT WINGED FOOT.

text.p: John Daly, Tiger Woods, Tom Kite and Justin Leonard among others feasted on birdies at rain-softened Winged Foot, but Britain's Nick Faldo and Darren Clarke failed to join the fun in Thursday's opening round of the PGA Championship.
Daly was the early first-round leader with a four-under-par 66, leaving triple Masters and British Open champion Faldo nine strokes behind, one worse than this year's British Open runner-up Clarke.
"I just played badly, as simple as that," grunted Faldo after an opening 75 that held six bogeys and one birdie. "Just a lot of off-shots. Off drives, off second shots. Simple as that."
Clarke had trouble off the tee -- guaranteed to produce misery given the severe rough and tiny, fast-sloping greens of Winged Foot.
"I can't remember the last time I played and didn't make a birdie," the Northern Irishman said after his 74. "It's been a long, long time."
The Britons were not the only name players in the 150-man field to struggle. Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, who shared second place at Royal Troon with Clarke, posted a six-over 76.
Two-time Masters champion Ben Crenshaw soared to a 77 and former PGA champion Hal Sutton had a 78, among others disappointed finishers.
Besides his poor form, Faldo was also unhappy after being addressed on two separate occasion by officials over slow play.
"We were out of position for 10 minutes. It happens all the time. No big deal," Faldo snapped before storming away from reporters.
